title: Active simplification backlog
status: Original proposals retained; limited search/reading/scope actions approved and implemented November 4; remaining choices open
review_method: Primary Codex agent inspected the current checked-in site template, generated page, UI code, documentation and build audit. No new sub-agents, human usability sessions, browser QA or runtime performance benchmarks were conducted.
priority_basis: Ian’s November 3 clarification: public audience first, Fellows/alumni second; easy archive navigation with prominent search and random discovery, machine-assisted synthesis, data quality and human interpretability. Design history is preserved in some form. No production simplification is approved. November 4: the separate approval record supersedes the earlier no-implementation status only for its bounded actions.

observed.measurement_limits: Static markup/data-size counts, not simultaneous visible controls, measured usability, load time or memory use.

tracking.owner: Ian G. Williams; assisting agents maintain this list within authorized tasks
tracking.review_trigger: Revisit during the next authorized revision plan, before adding another top-level feature, and at future release reviews. No scheduled automation is created.
tracking.rule: No item changes to approved or implementation solely because it is listed here. Keep stable IDs, rationale, decision, affected evidence and verification result; preserve historical decisions.
tracking.next_action: Review the interactive Welcoming pathways prototype and identify further revisions. Existing SIM items remain production proposals until separately approved.

items.component: Appearance lab and annual style controls
items.proposed_revision: Move to an optional design-history page; use a stable reading appearance in the main explorer. Retain readable type, contrast and comfortable spacing controls.
items.rationale: Fifteen annual presets, a year slider/select/step buttons, typography, surface, layout, spacing, color and strength controls plus settings download form a second product alongside archive research. They also create a distinction between design year and post year that readers must keep straight.
items.preserve: The design-history experiment was explicitly requested earlier. Retain its sources, saved presets and project-history account; do not erase this work.
items.decision_needed: Choose a discoverable but secondary design-history form; preserve the feature and sourced research, as Ian requested.
items.acceptance_criteria: A visitor can read, search and inspect evidence without encountering year-style controls; the optional exhibit and sources remain reachable.
items.confidence: Source inspection supports the described controls and structure; user-benefit estimates are hypotheses, not usability findings.

items.proposed_revision: Consolidate into approximately five destinations: Overview; Posts; Patterns; Methods & evidence; Credits & project history. Put topic/word/theme tools inside Patterns and technical checks inside Methods.
items.rationale: The current navigation gives reading, statistical diagnostics, report guidance and development history comparable prominence. A smaller set makes the task hierarchy clearer.
items.preserve: Preserve existing view/section links through aliases or redirects and keep credit/correction access obvious.
items.decision_needed: Approve grouping and labels before any navigation change.
items.acceptance_criteria: Existing bookmarks still open their intended content; a reviewer can find posts, methods and credits without guessing among diagnostic tabs.
items.confidence: Source inspection supports the described controls and structure; user-benefit estimates are hypotheses, not usability findings.

items.component: Long overview and repeated entry points
items.proposed_revision: Shorten the landing page to purpose, source/snapshot, brief status disclosure and three actions: browse posts, read the interpretation, inspect methods. Relocate the detailed process, repeated route lists and most scope definitions.
items.rationale: The overview source has 16 buttons plus multiple explanatory sections, in addition to the global navigation. Several routes repeat the same destination. The grouped-author count is harder to interpret than an archive size.
items.preserve: Keep a short AI/project-status notice, original-site link and correction route. Retain detailed population counts where they are used.
items.decision_needed: Choose a public-first orientation with search, random discovery and synthesis all readily available; compare the three mockup directions.
items.acceptance_criteria: The first screen gives a clear purpose and primary action; 421 published records and the snapshot remain clear without presenting grouped author entries as a verified headcount.
items.confidence: Source inspection supports the described controls and structure; user-benefit estimates are hypotheses, not usability findings.

items.proposed_revision: Show search, academic year and author first in the index. Place technical topic thresholds, record-status/type distinctions and membership evidence in a clearly labelled advanced area. Use consistent control wording and an always-visible active-filter/scope summary.
items.rationale: The index/network markup contains 11 selects plus text search; topics and themes expose different versions of authorship and membership controls. In topics/words, selecting a membership basis has no effect until a separate checkbox is checked. Themes has two overlapping credit checkboxes.
items.preserve: Retain all 430 records, draft metadata and all five membership bases. Preserve all/source-supported distinctions and guests. Do not force one global filter across incompatible analytical populations.
items.decision_needed: Approve a basic/advanced layout and, later, any proposed change to default record scope.
items.acceptance_criteria: Every applied filter is visible; controls change their advertised population; source-supported authorship remains distinct from fellowship membership and collective-post inclusion.
items.confidence: Source inspection supports the described controls and structure; user-benefit estimates are hypotheses, not usability findings.

items.component: Network open before post results, showing all authors
items.proposed_revision: Keep the author/year graph as an optional visualization, closed initially; put matching post results first. Offer the existing table as a direct alternative and render large graphs only when requested.
items.rationale: The index network disclosure is currently open and its default is All in this selection. This can place a large graph ahead of the archive results. Its table alternative is nested inside the graph section.
items.preserve: The network was explicitly requested and should remain available. Its edges count publication credits, not appointments, expertise or productivity.
items.decision_needed: Approve secondary placement rather than deletion.
items.acceptance_criteria: Search results are reachable before the graph; table and graph expose the same eligible credits, coauthor counting and unresolved-credit warnings.
items.confidence: Source inspection supports the described controls and structure; user-benefit estimates are hypotheses, not usability findings.

items.component: Standalone random-post route and separate reader tools
items.proposed_revision: Consolidate post reading with the searchable index and retain Draw a random post as an optional action there. Use one post-detail component with original link, credit evidence and expandable saved analysis.
items.rationale: Search currently links titles to original posts, while the internal reading copy and saved-analysis action live in the random reader. These are related tasks split between routes. Consolidation may require a deliberate post-by-ID reader entry point.
items.preserve: Random discovery and per-post analysis were explicitly requested. Preserve them as actions, including honest exclusions for unmodeled posts and plain-text/multimedia limits. Ian’s November 3 clarification makes random discovery a core task: it must remain prominent even if the reader is consolidated.
items.decision_needed: Approve one shared reader and retain random discovery as a secondary action.
items.acceptance_criteria: Any selected published post can be read with the same evidence tools; drafts remain metadata-only; random sampling stays documented and does not invent model results.
items.confidence: Source inspection supports the described controls and structure; user-benefit estimates are hypotheses, not usability findings.

items.component: Duplicate publication and keyword charts in the legacy audit route
items.proposed_revision: Retire the legacy audit view from primary navigation and link its preserved tables/charts from Methods. Use Themes as the primary place for interactive keyword comparisons.
items.rationale: Publishing & motifs includes publication mix, the older 307-post body analysis and original 325-post title/tag signals, alongside newer thematic views. Similar-looking charts have different populations and can look like interchangeable evidence.
items.preserve: Do not combine the 307- and 325-post measures or delete historical artifacts. Preserve their definitions, filenames and source tables.
items.decision_needed: Approve archival placement of legacy displays; any recalculation would be a separate decision.
items.acceptance_criteria: One obvious route serves each current comparison, and historical charts remain reproducible with their original denominators.
items.confidence: Source inspection supports the described controls and structure; user-benefit estimates are hypotheses, not usability findings.

items.component: Repeated methods, report guidance, histories and long disclosures
items.proposed_revision: Keep one concise methods hub, one contributor/AI disclosure, and linked report/reuse/history appendices. Replace repeated paragraphs with short context-specific caveats plus links to authoritative detail.
items.rationale: Overview, Methods, For reports, Credits, Project history, work log and standalone guides repeat portions of scope, AI provenance and process. Repetition creates reading burden and several places for old counts or wording to persist.
items.preserve: Do not remove CRediT/GAIDeT records, the source-author register, attribution decisions, correction contact, rights status or source evidence. Important warnings must remain at the point where a result could be misread.
items.decision_needed: Approve canonical document ownership and which material becomes an appendix.
items.acceptance_criteria: Each maintained claim has a canonical source; critical credit/denominator warnings are visible locally and full evidence remains at most one clearly labelled link away.
items.confidence: Source inspection supports the described controls and structure; user-benefit estimates are hypotheses, not usability findings.

items.component: Advanced statistics in ordinary exploration and every post profile
items.proposed_revision: Keep one primary model in ordinary views; place model-run choice, token weighting, seed stability, quality metrics and writer-exclusion sensitivity in a coherent advanced-research section.
items.rationale: Five saved runs, weighting choices and diagnostics have legitimate examination value, but most readers need first to understand a primary chart. Post-level model selectors repeat the run-selection task. Public-first orientation strengthens the case for progressive disclosure while preserving reviewer access.
items.preserve: Research/examination is the priority, so diagnostics remain accessible. Do not discard alternative runs, declare the default optimal or hide sensitivity limitations.
items.decision_needed: Approve advanced placement, not removal of statistical evidence.
items.acceptance_criteria: A novice can inspect a primary topic and its posts; an examiner can still compare all saved models and reproduce scope-specific results.
items.confidence: Source inspection supports the described controls and structure; user-benefit estimates are hypotheses, not usability findings.

items.component: Several thematic charts competing on one page
items.proposed_revision: Lead with the theme/year view and supporting post list. Make co-occurrence and writer bars optional secondary analyses rather than presenting every chart at equal prominence.
items.rationale: The thematic route contains a heatmap, pair matrix, writer bars, evidence cards and multiple exports. This supports several different questions and requires readers to understand both global filters and selections affecting only evidence lists.
items.preserve: Preserve the distinction among keyword layers, the selected essay examples and MALLET topics. Retain overlap counts, denominators and original author/source evidence.
items.decision_needed: Choose the default thematic question and chart hierarchy.
items.acceptance_criteria: The active question and the scope of a cell/pair selection are explicit; secondary analyses reproduce their current counts when opened.
items.confidence: Source inspection supports the described controls and structure; user-benefit estimates are hypotheses, not usability findings.

items.component: Phrase statistics and fixed early/recent comparison in the word route
items.proposed_revision: Keep basic word counts visible and place phrase association measures and fixed-period contrasts behind an advanced disclosure or in Methods.
items.rationale: Word filters apply to one chart, while phrase scores always describe the 299-post corpus and contrasts use fixed periods. Multiple association measures are useful to specialists but increase explanation and filter-scope burden.
items.preserve: Retain saved PMI/log-likelihood tables, thresholds and fixed-period definitions. Do not pretend these tools obey filters they do not use.
items.decision_needed: Approve secondary placement; assess whether the fixed-period contrast still answers a current research question.
items.acceptance_criteria: It is clear which views respond to filters; specialist measures remain reproducible and no comparison silently changes population.
items.confidence: Source inspection supports the described controls and structure; user-benefit estimates are hypotheses, not usability findings.

items.component: Multiple export/control actions with limited primary-task value
items.proposed_revision: Prioritize matching-post CSVs, displayed chart-table exports and stable source/view links. Consider retiring appearance-settings JSON and redundant chart copies from the main interface while preserving archived files.
items.rationale: Data/evidence exports support examination. Downloading appearance configuration and carrying design settings in shared links add maintenance to a secondary design experiment. Shared links currently omit research filters and selected posts.
items.preserve: Preserve scientific downloads, stable original links and explicit share limitations. Do not label a view-only URL as a saved research selection or add personal filter serialization without review.
items.decision_needed: Approve which exports are primary; design-setting export can remain with the optional design exhibit if retained.
items.acceptance_criteria: A reader can export the evidence they see and understand exactly what a shared link preserves.
items.confidence: Source inspection supports the described controls and structure; user-benefit estimates are hypotheses, not usability findings.

items.component: One large offline page embedding several datasets and all feature code
items.proposed_revision: Investigate a lighter web entry point and clearer module ownership only after the visible hierarchy is simplified. Keep an explicit self-contained offline research package as an alternative.
items.rationale: The current HTML is 5,421,440 bytes and embeds explorer, index, reader, theme and style data. This is a maintenance/duplication candidate, not evidence of slow load times; no new runtime benchmark was performed.
items.preserve: Offline/shareable behavior and source/model preservation are intentional. Splitting files can break direct-file use, stable links or no-network operation and is not an automatic improvement.
items.decision_needed: Decide whether a separate lightweight web edition is worth maintaining; benchmark representative tasks first.
items.acceptance_criteria: Any future architecture change is supported by measured benefit and preserves an independently verified offline package, dataset fingerprints and current attribution joins.
items.confidence: Source inspection supports the described controls and structure; user-benefit estimates are hypotheses, not usability findings.

stages.name: Approve scope
stages.gate: Compare Open library, Collective wisdom and Welcoming pathways (or a deliberate blend); agree public orientation, prominent search/random/synthesis tasks and a preserved optional design-history form.

stages.name: Reduce visible complexity
stages.gate: Authorize a small reversible pass with source/credit/denominator safeguards; verify old links and unchanged counts.

stages.name: Consolidate related tools
stages.gate: Review focused component plans and test existing/guest/unmodeled/draft/curated cases before an authorized release.

stages.name: Measure before architectural change
stages.gate: Benchmark and confirm continued offline requirements; obtain separate approval for any architecture change.

contribution.ai: OpenAI Codex performed source inspection and static inventory, drafted prioritized hypotheses, tradeoffs, acceptance criteria and this planning record. Exact underlying model/build is not recorded.
contribution.oversight: Proposals await Ian’s decisions; no participant user study was conducted.

scope: Source drilldowns and complete author tables

approved.reading: Excerpts with full in-depth in-app reading options
approved.public_scope: 421 published records by default; nine drafts remain metadata-only through research/accounting

approval_updates.related_implementation: Focus/return paths, matched snippets, source-rights propagation, post results before the collapsed network, and preview heading/skip improvements. Existing production layout retained; five-route prototype is a separate preview.
open_decisions: Whether design history restyles the whole application or only a preview
approval_updates.not_authorized_by_unanswered_questions: No new network/evidence default, synthesis rename, design-history policy, human recruitment or production replacement inferred.

approved.network: Offer toggles for all years/names or a selected year/person, independently combined with all recorded credits or source-supported credits. Preserve visible uncertainty and denominators.
approved.synthesis: Use the more tentative title What the archive suggests, retaining the 19-selected-post and AI-assistance qualifications.
approved.design_history: Apply the selected design era across the whole explorer application, including navigation and reading. Preserve data, route identifiers and accessibility overrides.
approved.human_evaluation: Human-review availability is limited; scheduling, support and scope TBD. No new evaluation session or participants established.

approval_updates.limits: Network filters reaggregate saved publication credits; they do not verify authorship, fellowship appointments, productivity or collaboration. Whole-application appearance means internal explorer views, not external original posts or separately opened reference documents. No institutional endorsement or comprehensive human validation is inferred.
approval_updates.remaining: Human evaluation arrangements; separate approval still required to replace the production layout with the five-destination preview.
